subject: Proxy processing carve-outs under UK Addendum — Helix Health
messages:
From: Sophia Lam <sophia.lam@helixhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proxy processing carve-outs under UK Addendum — Helix Health

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our call today. A follow-up from legal: Helix runs a set of analytics and third-party enrichment flows that proxy-process some UK-derived data in the US and Canada for fraud detection and de‑duplication. Our counsel is concerned that the standard UK Addendum (IDTA) language would effectively prohibit those flows unless we list them as explicit carve-outs or provide an alternative safeguard.

Can Redwood confirm:
- Whether you can support a limited proxy-processing carve-out in the UK Addendum that lists specific categories of processing (analytics, fraud, enrichment) and the subprocessors involved.
- What technical routing guarantees you can provide (e.g., region tag + fallback behavior) and how those interact with the TIA/DTIA scope.
- Evidence we can share with our legal team (TIAs, SOC2, ingress/egress logging) while we negotiate the DPA addendum redline.

I've attached our question set (Helix_Questions.xlsx). If you can propose suggested language for a carve-out and a short TIA summary that shows controls for those activities, that would speed review.

Sophia Lam
Head of Legal Operations
Helix Health

Attachment: Helix_Questions.xlsx (spreadsheet - 14KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Lam <sophia.lam@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Helix Health Legal <legal@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proxy processing carve-outs under UK Addendum — Helix Health

Sophia — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. We can support a tightly scoped carve-out subject to (i) listing the specific processing categories, (ii) a subprocessors list and (iii) an updated TIA that documents compensating technical controls.

High-level proposals we will provide by end-of-day tomorrow:
- Suggested DPA addendum wording you can drop into your redline that enumerates the carve-outs (analytics: fraud detection, dedupe, enrichment).
- A one-page Redwood_TIA_Summary.pdf that maps controls to the carve-out (routing, encryption in transit at TLS1.3, HSM-wrapped keys for exported artifacts, prefix/KV caching exclusion where needed).
- A proxy-processing-mapping.csv that lists the subprocessors and the precise data elements that may transit outside the UK.

Routing guarantees: we offer a region-tagging policy where requests originating from the UK are routed to EU/UK-capable clusters by default. For the carve-out, we would mark those specific flows as "conditional proxy" and allow them to traverse the US/CAN with the following constraints:
  * Data minimization rules (strip PHI fields; pseudonymize IDs)
  * Access controls: subprocessors on allowlist only, with role-based access and short-lived creds
  * Full request/response logging with ingress/egress retention for 90 days (can extend via contract)
  * Automatic fallback: if EU capacity unavailable, requests queue for up to 30s or fall back to a lower-privilege on-prem processing profile (per your preference)

We will upload the TIA summary and mapping now and set up a short review call. Tagging Priyom and Logan for technical details.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_TIA_Summary.pdf (PDF - 23KB); proxy-processing-mapping.csv (CSV - 6KB)

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Sophia Lam <sophia.lam@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proxy processing carve-outs under UK Addendum — Helix Health

Sophia / Kimberly — quick technical addendum to clarify how routing and fallback will behave in practice.

1) Region tags and routing policy
   - Requests carry an explicit origin-region header. For standard sessions from the UK, routing selects eu/uk pools.
   - For the permitted proxy flows we propose a named routing-class "helix-proxy-analytics". That class can be bound to a small set of US/CAN pools and is visible in the console for auditing.

2) Data-class transformations
   - Before any cross-border transfer we will apply the configured transform pipeline: hash(person_id), remove_direct_identifiers, and redact free-text excerpts matching PHI regexes. We will include the transformation log as part of the TIA artifact.

3) Subprocessor lifecycle and attestations
   - We will provide the current subprocessor snapshot and include an audit snapshot (S3 presigned) for the last 90 days of access events for each subprocess.
   - If Helix requires weekly attestations during the onboarding window, we can commit to a 6-week cadence while you conclude legal redlines.

4) Operational fallbacks
   - If eu/uk capacity hits latency SLO thresholds, the system will either (A) queue requests for up to 30s for prioritised processing in eu/uk, or (B) route to helix-proxy-analytics class depending on your tolerance.

I'll attach a mapping CSV that pairs each subprocess with the exact data elements that may be processed outside the UK. Happy to run a screen-share to walk through the audit artifacts.

—Logan
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proxy-processing-mapping.csv (CSV - 6KB)

Kimberly / team — this is helpful, thanks. Our outside counsel reviewed the proposed carve-out language and the TIA summary and have two asks before we can approve moving the clause into the redline: 

1) Add an explicit maximum retention period for transformation logs and ingress/egress logs (legal proposes 180 days for operational logs, archive with further approval).
2) A short example clause that says Helix may require temporary onshore-only processing for specific datasets during incident response.

If you can produce (A) the DPA addendum snippet we can insert, (B) a one-paragraph incident-response onshore-processing clause, and (C) the 90-day audit snapshot link, we can circulate to internal procurement and finalize next week.

We appreciate the operational fallbacks — the routing-class concept should work for us. Please send the redline language and the snapshot link; procurement will also want a short note on support escalation SLAs for the helix-proxy-analytics class.

Sophia Lam
Head of Legal Operations
Helix Health
